main_text.p: effatum oftentat, Galenus, qui illi Doctor irrefragabilis, atque Ariftote-les reprobant. Galenus quidem lib. 5. de usu partium, cap. 3. inquiens "Ἐνίοις ἐδέμιλαν χρείαν γίνεσθαι, ἀλλ' ἐπέρχεσ ἐξ ἀνάγ-κης ἕπεσθαι, ἃ δὲ μέρεα εἶναι, ἀλλὰ τινὰ σύμ-πλοκα, quædam fieri nullius usus gratia, sed sequi quædam alia, quæ fiunt necessa-riò, non ut partes, sed ut quædam simul concincidentia. Et paulò post ait, hinc intelligitur, hanc quidem primorum in-volucrorum inanitionem nullius usus causa exstitisse, quod & alibi dixerat. Aristoteles verò 8. Metaph. cap. 4. ubi inquirens in causam Eclipseos nullam illius agnoscit materiam præter lunam quæ patitur: causa autem agens & corrumpens lumen lunæ illi est terra, τὰ δὲ ἐξ ἕνεκα ἵνας οὐκ ἐστι[?], at causa finalis hîc nulla est. Et certè vana & fallax est sententia Doctoris Le Vasseur, si putet nihil frustra fieri, significare, omnia intendere finem, uti sunt quàm plurimi, eodem lacte, quo Le Vasseur, enutri-ti,

page.notes: The Greek lines are partly cut off at the left edge and are transcribed from the visible letters; the Greek of the first quotation and of the line beginning "τὰ δὲ" is uncertain. The Latin words at the left edge are cropped and were read from their visible ends, so the beginnings of some lines may be incomplete.
